comments.headline: Landscape plan lacks species identification and maturity data
comments.summary: Plant schedule provides species names and quantities but omits utility-compatible (UC) status and mature heights. Species are not labeled on landscape plan symbols, preventing verification of UC designation and large tree (40+ feet) clearance requirements.

details.text: Plant schedule lists species (Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Mexican Redbud, Texas Mountain Laurel) but does not document utility-compatible (UC) designation per ECM Appendix F. Cannot verify that all trees within 15 feet of distribution conductors are UC-designated.

runComments.comment: Plant schedule lists tree species (Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Mexican Redbud, Texas Mountain Laurel) but does not indicate utility-compatible (UC) designation per ECM Appendix F. Cannot verify whether proposed trees are UC-designated or not. Applicant must cross-reference all species against ECM Appendix F UC column and confirm all trees within 15 feet of distribution conductor are utility-compatible.

Proposed non-utility-compatible trees (Cedar Elm, Live Oak) are shown on the landscape plan near the overhead electric distribution line on the southern boundary. The plant schedule does not identify UC (utility-compatible) status for any tree species, and no clearance dimensions or measurements are provided on the plans to verify compliance with the 15 lateral foot minimum clearance for non-UC trees from distribution conductors. Compliance cannot be verified without documented UC designations and clearance dimensions.

Landscape plan shows trees planted 5-10 feet from overhead electric distribution lines along southern and western property boundaries, but does not identify species of individual trees. Plant schedule lists species (Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Mexican Redbud, Texas Mountain Laurel) with total quantities but does not indicate which species are planted at which locations. Cannot verify whether non-utility-compatible trees (Cedar Elm and Live Oak are non-UC species) are within 15-foot restricted zone without species identification on plan drawing.

details.text: Landscape plan symbols (M for mitigation, SY/ST for street yard, P for parking, PL for parking lot) lack species identification. Plant schedule lists species and quantities separately but does not cross-reference which species correspond to each symbol on the drawing.

runComments.comment: Landscape plan shows tree locations using symbol designations (M, SY, PL, P) without species identification. Plant schedule on Sheet 35 lists species and quantities separately but does not cross-reference which species correspond to each symbol on the landscape plan. Reviewers cannot verify species identity, utility compatibility, or maturity height for specific tree locations. Applicant must either label trees on landscape plan with species names or add legend clearly linking each landscape symbol to specific species in plant schedule.

Landscape plan uses functional classification symbols (M for mitigation tree, SY for street yard tree, ST for street yard tree, P for parking buffer point, PL for parking lot tree) but does not identify species for any proposed trees shown on the drawing. Plant schedule (Sheet 35) lists species and quantities separately but does not show where each species is planted on the landscape plan. Reviewer cannot cross-reference specific tree symbols on the landscape plan to species identification.

details.text: Plant schedule provides only minimum planting container heights (e.g., 16' HT minimum) and does not document mature heights for any species. Cannot determine which species are large trees (40+ feet per ECM Appendix F) or verify 25-foot lateral clearance from distribution conductors.

runComments.comment: Plant schedule provides species names and minimum container heights (e.g., 16' HT minimum for nursery stock), but does not provide mature height at maturity for any species. Cannot determine which species are large trees (40+ feet per ECM Appendix F maturity classification). Applicant must provide mature height for each tree species and verify no large trees within 25 feet of distribution conductor.

Live Oak (Quercus virginiana) is proposed on the site plan with a mature height of 40-50+ feet, qualifying as a large tree per UCM § 1.10.10.4 and ECM Appendix F. The plant schedule on Sheet 35 does not document mature heights for proposed trees—it shows only minimum planting specifications (16' HT minimum). Large trees cannot be differentiated on the plans, and no clearance dimensions are provided to verify the required 25 lateral foot minimum distance from distribution conductors. All proposed large trees must be clearly marked on the landscape plan with mature height notation to allow verification of overhead clearance compliance.

Large trees (Cedar Elm and Live Oak, with mature heights 40+ feet) are proposed within 5-10 feet of overhead distribution lines, inside the 25-foot clearance zone. However, plant schedule does not provide mature height specifications—only container-grown minimums (16' HT minimum). Large trees are not differentiated on landscape plan to allow verification of 25-foot clearances from distribution conductors. Without mature height data and species identification on the landscape plan, compliance cannot be verified.

details.text: Large trees (Cedar Elm at 40-50 ft, Live Oak at 40-80 ft mature height per ECM Appendix F) are not differentiated on the landscape plan. Plant schedule shows only container minimums (16' HT) rather than mature heights and does not indicate which trees are large (40+ feet).

runComments.comment: Landscape plan does not differentiate large trees (mature height 40+ feet per ECM Appendix F). Plant schedule provides species names but no mature height values. Cannot determine which, if any, proposed species mature to 40+ feet or whether such trees are positioned outside the 25-foot clearance zone from distribution conductors. Applicant must provide mature height for each tree species and use notation or symbol on landscape plan to identify all trees that mature to 40+ feet.

The plant schedule provides minimum planting height specifications (e.g., 16' HT minimum for Live Oak, 10' HT for Mexican Redbud) but does not provide mature height information required to identify large trees (40+ feet per ECM Appendix F). Large trees cannot be differentiated on the landscape plan or in the plant schedule. The mature height for each species must be documented in the plant schedule to allow verification of clearance compliance with overhead electric facilities.

Large trees (Cedar Elm at 40-50 ft mature height, Live Oak at 40-80 ft mature height per ECM Appendix F) are not differentiated on the landscape plan. Plant schedule shows only container-grown minimum heights (16' HT minimum) rather than mature heights, and does not indicate which trees are large (40+ feet). Large trees require enhanced clearances (25 feet from distribution, 50 feet from transmission) and must be clearly identified on plans to allow clearance verification.

details.text: Landscape and electrical plans are not cross-referenced with dimension callouts or notes documenting the spatial relationship between proposed trees and electrical infrastructure. Clearance compliance cannot be verified without linked documentation.

runComments.comment: The landscape plan shows proposed trees adjacent to the overhead electric line on the southern site boundary, but the relationship between trees and electric infrastructure is not documented. No clearance dimensions, callouts, reference notes, or cross-references link the landscape plan to the electrical plan to verify compliance with overhead electric clearance requirements. Plans must clearly show the spatial relationship between proposed trees and overhead electric facilities with documented clearance verification.

comments.headline: Missing clearance dimension callouts from electrical infrastructure
comments.summary: Landscape plan lacks dimensioned callouts verifying clearances from proposed trees to overhead conductors, utility poles, transformer pads, and underground equipment. Clearance compliance cannot be verified without documented dimensions measured from tree trunks and conductor/pole/equipment locations.
comments.crossDep: Austin Energy (utility department) must verify clearance measurements or provide written approval for any variances from minimum clearance zones.
comments.attn: Dimension callouts required showing clearance distances from: (1) overhead conductors, (2) tree trunk centers, (3) utility poles, (4) transformer pads, (5) underground pull boxes.

details.text: No dimension callouts or measurement annotations appear on the landscape plan showing clearance distances between proposed trees and overhead electric conductors. Clearance measurements must be taken from the outside edge of conductors (not pole centerline) and documented on the plan.

runComments.comment: No dimension callouts or measurement annotations are provided on the landscape plan to show clearance distances between proposed trees and the overhead electric conductors. Cannot verify whether any clearance measurements are taken from the outside edge of conductors (as required) rather than from pole centerline.

details.text: No dimension callouts terminate at tree trunk centers showing clearance measurements. Clearance distances must be measured from tree trunk locations (not from the edge of projected canopies) and verified on the plan.

runComments.comment: Trees on landscape plan are shown as circular canopy symbols with trunk center points. No dimension callouts terminate at tree trunk centers to show clearance measurements. Cannot verify whether clearance distances are measured from tree trunk locations (as required) rather than from the edge of projected canopies.

details.text: At least one mitigation tree is positioned 5-8 feet from an existing overhead electric utility pole on the southern boundary, placing it within the prohibited 10-foot lateral clearance zone. Required minimum clearance from tree trunk to pole is 10 feet; clearance dimensions are not documented on the plan.

runComments.comment: At least one mitigation tree (M) is positioned 5-8 feet from an existing overhead electric utility pole on the southern boundary, placing it within the prohibited 10-foot clearance zone. All trees must be positioned minimum 10 feet (lateral distance from trunk to pole) from utility poles. Relocate tree or provide documented Austin Energy written approval.

The electrical design plan shows utility poles as nodal points along existing overhead electric lines. The landscape plan shows proposed trees throughout the site, including near site boundaries where poles are located. However, neither the electrical plan nor the landscape plan documents the precise locations of poles or provides clearance dimensions to the proposed trees. The required 10 lateral foot minimum clearance from tree trunks to utility poles cannot be verified without explicit pole locations and clearance measurements.

Overhead electric lines on western and southern property boundaries are supported by poles; landscape plan shows trees 5-10 feet from these conductor lines. Without dimension callouts showing distances from proposed trees to specific pole locations and without pole positions clearly marked on the landscape plan, cannot verify that all trees maintain minimum 10-foot clearance from pole centerlines.

details.text: Pad-mounted electrical transformers at four locations (west of Buildings 1 and 2, east of Building 5, south of Building 6) have proposed trees nearby without documented 10 lateral foot minimum clearance. No dimension callouts show clearance distances from trees to transformer pad equipment on the landscape plan.

runComments.comment: Electrical transformer pads are shown on electrical plan (Sheet 21) and trees are shown on landscape plan (Sheet 31), but the landscape plan does not indicate underground electrical equipment locations or dimensioned clearances. Cannot verify that trees are minimum 10 feet from pad-mounted equipment or that no trees are positioned between equipment access doors and drivable surfaces. Applicant must show transformer pad locations on landscape plan with dimensioned clearances from proposed trees.

Pad-mounted electrical transformers are shown at four locations on the electrical design plan. The landscape plan shows proposed trees throughout the site. However, no clearance dimensions are provided between any proposed trees and the transformer pads. The required 10 lateral foot minimum clearance from tree trunks to pad-mounted equipment cannot be verified without documented clearance measurements.

Electrical transformer pads and pull boxes are located near the western and southern property boundaries where trees are proposed. Electrical plan shows transformer pad west of Building 1, 2, and 8, and pull box near southern boundary. Landscape plan shows trees in these areas but provides no dimension callouts verifying that proposed trees maintain minimum 10-foot clearance from pad-mounted equipment access doors.

details.text: Underground electrical pull boxes are shown on the electrical plan but not indicated on the landscape plan with clearance dimensions. The required 5 lateral foot minimum clearance from tree trunks to underground electrical equipment cannot be verified without documented measurements.

runComments.comment: Electrical pull boxes are shown on electrical plan but not indicated on landscape plan with distances to proposed trees. Cannot verify that trees are minimum 5 feet from underground electrical equipment. Applicant must show pull box and underground equipment locations on landscape plan with dimensioned clearances from all proposed trees.

The electrical design plan shows underground electric lines, pull boxes, and conduit routing throughout the site. The landscape plan shows numerous proposed trees, including in areas adjacent to underground utility routing. However, no clearance dimensions are provided between proposed trees and underground electrical equipment. The required 5 lateral foot minimum clearance from tree trunks to underground electric equipment cannot be verified without documented clearance measurements.

comments.headline: Root barrier specifications missing for underground equipment protection
comments.summary: Trees proposed within 20 feet of underground electrical equipment lack documented root barrier specifications required by UCM § 1.10.10.4. Root barriers (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned 5 feet from equipment) must be detailed on the landscape plan.
comments.attn: Applicant must identify all trees within 20 lateral feet of underground electrical equipment and detail 4-foot minimum depth root barriers positioned 5 feet from equipment on landscape plan detail sheets.

details.text: Trees are proposed throughout the site with underground electrical equipment (pull boxes, conduits) routing through landscaped areas. For any trees within 20 lateral feet of underground electrical equipment, minimum 4-foot deep root barriers positioned 5 feet from equipment are required. Landscape plan detail sheets and plant specifications contain no root barrier details or callouts.

runComments.comment: Without documented locations and distances of underground electrical equipment relative to proposed trees, cannot verify root barrier requirements for trees within 20 feet of underground equipment. Root barriers (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned 5 feet from equipment) must be detailed for any trees within 20 feet. Applicant must identify trees within 20 feet of underground equipment and specify root barrier details on landscape plan.

Trees are proposed throughout the site, and underground electrical equipment is shown on the electrical design plan. For any trees proposed within 20 lateral feet of underground electrical equipment, minimum 4-foot deep root barriers positioned 5 feet from equipment are required. The landscape plan contains no specifications, details, or callouts indicating that root barriers are provided. This requirement must be documented on the landscape plan with detail specifications.

Underground electric lines are shown routing through landscaped areas and past pull box locations. Landscape plan details (Sheet 37) show standard tree planting specifications but contain no root barrier details. Cannot verify whether root barriers (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned 5 feet from equipment) are specified for trees proposed within 20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment.

comments.headline: No Austin Energy written approval for restricted clearance zone plantings
comments.summary: Proposed trees are located within restricted clearance zones adjacent to overhead and underground electrical infrastructure. No documented written approval from Austin Energy authorizing these plantings in prohibited zones is provided with the application.
comments.crossDep: Austin Energy (utility provider) must issue written approval/variance letter for any trees proposed within restricted clearance zones.
comments.attn: Applicant must either (1) relocate all trees to comply with minimum clearances (10 feet from poles, 15 feet from non-UC trees, 25 feet from large trees from distribution conductors), or (2) obtain executed written approval from Austin Energy explicitly authorizing plantings in restricted zones.

details.text: Proposed trees are located within restricted clearance zones (5-10 feet from overhead distribution conductors and utility poles, within 25-foot clearance from large trees). No executed written approval from Austin Energy authorizing restricted zone plantings is visible on the site plan or supplementary documents.

runComments.comment: At least one mitigation tree (M) is positioned 5-8 feet from an existing overhead electric utility pole on the southern boundary, placing it within the prohibited 10-foot clearance zone. All trees must be positioned minimum 10 feet (lateral distance from trunk to pole) from utility poles. Plans do not include documented written approval from Austin Energy authorizing this exception. Applicant must either relocate the tree to comply with minimum 10-foot clearance or provide executed written approval letter from Austin Energy explicitly authorizing the variance.

Proposed trees appear to be located within clearance-restricted zones (adjacent to overhead conductors, near transformer pads, near underground equipment). No documented written approval from Austin Energy authorizing these plantings within restricted zones is visible on the site plan or in supplementary documents. All trees proposed within restricted clearance zones must include explicit written approval from Austin Energy, or plantings must be relocated to compliant locations.

Proposed trees are located within the restricted clearance zones adjacent to overhead electric distribution lines (5-10 feet from the OHE line). No written approval from Austin Energy is provided or referenced in the site plan documents to authorize tree placement within these prohibited zones. Variations to planting distances and species near utility facilities require explicit written approval from Austin Energy.
